mainTopic: The hanging limb and the rule that מיתה makes it count as fallen off but שחיטה does not; how שחיטה works for a fetus (בן שמונה, בן תשעה, בן פקועה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a hanging limb of a properly שחוט animal is forbidden only by a rabbinic מצוה to keep away. רב יוסף then quotes רב that eating a hanging limb brings מלקות, while another Sage quotes רב the opposite way. רב יוסף explains that both quotes are right: מיתה makes the limb count as fallen off (ניפול), so it is אבר מן החי, but שחיטה does not. רבא finds the source for this in the extra word בְּמֹתָם, which is written twice in the פסוקים about שרצים. רב חסדא and רבה then disagree about whether the מחלוקת in the משנה about a fetus's limb covers a dead fetus too. Next, the גמרא settles a clash between the משנה and a ברייתא about a live בן שמונה, and shows how the ברייתא learns that a slaughtered טרפה is טהור. רב הושעיא asks whether slaughtering a live nine-month fetus inside its mother works, and רבא pushes away the proof brought for it. Finally, a new משנה rules on a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal: רבי מאיר says a live nine-month fetus needs its own שחיטה, while the חכמים say its mother's שחיטה is enough.

steps.title: Only a rabbinic duty to keep away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion: the hanging limb and flesh of a שחוט animal carry only a מצוה to keep away from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: With them there is only a מצוה to separate oneself.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion that began before this section. The גמרא concludes that after a proper שחיטה, a hanging limb is not forbidden by the Torah. There is only a rabbinic מצוה to stay away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that שחיטה does not turn the hanging limb into אבר מן החי. So the Torah does not forbid it. The rabbis still tell us to keep away from it, and that is the only prohibition left.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing with them except
A מצוה to separate oneself (a rabbinic duty to keep away)

steps.whatToRemember: After שחיטה, a hanging limb is only rabbinically forbidden (מצות פרוש). It is not forbidden by the Torah.

phrases.english: There is nothing with them except
phrases.notes: "Them" means the hanging limb and hanging flesh of an animal that was properly slaughtered, from the discussion just before.

phrases.english: a מצוה to separate oneself, only.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בָּהֶן אֶלָּא מִצְוַת פְּרוֹשׁ בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A hanging limb of a שחוט animal is forbidden only by a rabbinic מצוה to keep away.

steps.title: רב יוסף quotes רב: eating the hanging limb brings lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, sitting before רב הונא, quotes רב יהודה in the name of רב: someone who eats the hanging limb gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף sat before רב הונא and said: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: One who eats this hanging limb is flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. רב יוסף reports a ruling from רב that someone who eats a hanging limb gets מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות means a Torah prohibition was broken. So this ruling treats the hanging limb as אבר מן החי. The ruling does not say what kind of case it means, and that gap matters in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat before Rav Huna,
and he sat and was saying:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If he ate this one, he is flogged.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the hanging limb the גמרא has been talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the hanging limb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the name of רב: one who eats a hanging limb gets מלקות.

steps.title: A Sage quotes רב the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed Sage says not to listen to רב יוסף, because רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא quoted רב as saying there are no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said: Do not listen to him. This is what רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: One who eats this is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: Another Sage challenges רב יוסף's quote. He brings a different report of רב's words that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two reports of what רב said, and they clash: "flogged" and "not flogged." The Sage assumes רב יוסף's version must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the Sages

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to him:
Do not listen to him,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: this is what Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said
in the name of Rav:
If he ate this one, he is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the quote in step 2 with an opposite version of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's report that רב said one gets מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different reliable chain quotes רב as saying there are no מלקות, so רב יוסף's version seems wrong.

steps.title: רב הונא asks which version to follow
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks רב יוסף which report of רב's ruling we should rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: On whom shall we rely?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא sees two reports that clash, and he asks which one to follow. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא is not taking a side. He wants to know how to rule in practice when two quotes of the same teacher disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
We, on whom shall we rely?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן אַמַּאן נִסְמוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to decide between the two reports in steps 2 and 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of רב's ruling should be followed in practice.

steps.title: Both versions are right: death versus slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that there is no clash. His version is about מיתה, which makes the limb count as fallen off. The other version is about שחיטה, which does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף turned his face away and said: What is the difficulty? When I said it, it was about death, which makes the limb count as fallen off. When he said it, it was about slaughter, which does not make it count as fallen off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף, upset, explains that both reports of רב are true because they talk about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal dies without שחיטה, its death makes the hanging limb count as if it fell off while the animal was alive. That makes it אבר מן החי, so there are מלקות. If the animal is שחוט, the שחיטה does not do this, so there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned his face away (in annoyance)
Makes it count as fallen off

steps.whatToRemember: מיתה עושה ניפול: death makes a hanging limb count as fallen off while the animal was alive. שחיטה אינה עושה ניפול: slaughter does not.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not taking back his quote, and he is not saying the other quote is wrong. Both are accurate quotes of רב, and each one is about a different case.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef turned his face away,
he said to him: What is the difficulty?
When I said it, it was about death,
which makes it fallen off;
phrases.notes: He means death makes the limb count as if it fell off while the animal was still alive.

phrases.english: when he said it, it was about slaughter,
which does not make it fallen off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? כִּי אֲמַרִי אֲנָא – בְּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question and settles the clash from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each report is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two quotes of רב contradict each other, so one of them must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are correct. Eating the limb brings מלקות after מיתה, but not after שחיטה.

steps.title: רבא asks for the source of the death and slaughter rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where we learn the rule that מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off and שחיטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do we know this thing the Sages said: death makes it fallen off, slaughter does not make it fallen off?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the Torah source of the rule רב יוסף just used. This sets up the proof from a פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 used this rule without a source. רבא now wants to anchor it in a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From where is this matter that the Sages said:
death makes it fallen off,
slaughter does not make it fallen off,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָא מִלְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the rule used in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches מיתה עושה ניפול and שחיטה אינה עושה ניפול.

steps.title: The verse about creeping creatures: "when they are dead"
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק about שרצים, "in their death," and asks what the word בְּמֹתָם comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And anything that any of them falls on, in their death, shall be impure." What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes the פסוק he will use as the source. He asks what the extra word בְּמֹתָם comes to teach, which sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on showing that the word בְּמֹתָם is not needed for its simple meaning. If it is extra, it must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And anything that falls on it
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32

phrases.english: from them, in their death, shall be impure,"
to exclude what?
phrases.notes: He is asking what the word "in their death" comes to leave out.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל עָלָיו מֵהֶם בְּמֹתָם יִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the פסוק as the answer to רבא's question in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that מיתה עושה ניפול and שחיטה אינה עושה ניפול

steps.title: It cannot just exclude live creatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the simple reading that בְּמֹתָם excludes live שרצים, because we already learn that from the word נִבְלָתָם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it excludes when they are alive, that is already learned from "their carcass."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the obvious meaning of the word and rejects it. That meaning is already taught elsewhere, so this word would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק already says that only their נבלה, their dead body, makes things impure. So "in their death" cannot be there just to leave out live creatures. It must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived (we already learn it)

phrases.english: If you say it is to exclude when they are alive,
that is derived from "their carcass,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:35

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי בְּחַיֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects one possible answer to the question in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading that בְּמֹתָם simply excludes live creatures.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That lesson is already taught by נִבְלָתָם, so the word would be extra.

steps.title: So death makes it fallen off, slaughter does not
steps.stepSummary: Since בְּמֹתָם is not needed for its simple meaning, it teaches that מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off and שחיטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: death makes it fallen off, and slaughter does not make it fallen off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes רבא's proof. The extra word בְּמֹתָם is the source for the rule about death and slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks specifically of death. So the effect of making the limb count as fallen off belongs to death alone and not to שחיטה. This backs up רב יוסף's answer in step 5.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא learns from the word בְּמֹתָם that מיתה עושה ניפול and שחיטה אינה עושה ניפול. This is the basis for giving מלקות for a hanging limb after death but not after שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical difference: a hanging limb of a נבלה can bring מלקות as אבר מן החי, while a hanging limb of a שחוט animal has only a rabbinic prohibition (step 1).

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
death makes it fallen off,
and slaughter does not make it fallen off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the simple reading is rejected in step 8, draws the real lesson from the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word בְּמֹתָם teaches that מיתה makes a hanging limb count as fallen off, while שחיטה does not.

steps.title: But that verse is about creeping animals
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא: the פסוק of בְּמֹתָם is about שרצים, so how can it teach a rule about שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: But that verse is written about creeping animals!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks the proof from Step 9. He points out that the פסוק is talking about שרצים, not about animals that need שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned from בְּמֹתָם that מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off and שחיטה does not. But שרצים never get שחיטה at all. So how can a פסוק about them teach anything about שחיטה?

keyTerms.meaning: Small creeping creatures, such as mice and lizards, that make things impure when dead

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
But this verse is written about creeping animals!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק with בְּמֹתָם from Step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קְרָא בִּשְׁרָצִים כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in the conclusion of Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of בְּמֹתָם to teach a rule about שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is about שרצים, which have no שחיטה, so it cannot teach a difference between מיתה and שחיטה

steps.title: If it cannot apply to creeping animals, apply it to animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: since the teaching cannot apply to שרצים, which have no שחיטה, we move it over to a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it cannot be about creeping animals, since they do not get slaughtered, apply it to the case of an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. Since this lesson cannot be about שרצים, we apply it to a בהמה, which does get שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule of אם אינו ענין: when a word in a פסוק has no job in its own topic, we use it for a related topic. The word בְּמֹתָם is extra for שרצים, and a lesson about שחיטה makes no sense for them. So the lesson goes to בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this topic, apply it to another topic. This is a rule for using an extra word in a פסוק
Subject to slaughter; creatures that can be made permitted through שחיטה
A domestic animal, such as a cow, sheep or goat

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the פסוק stops being about שרצים. He is saying that the extra lesson inside the word בְּמֹתָם gets moved to בהמה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of creeping animals,
since they are not subject to slaughter,
apply it to the matter of an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לִשְׁרָצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the extra lesson to a related topic (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק is about שרצים, it cannot teach anything about שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the lesson cannot fit שרצים, it is applied to בהמה, which does get שחיטה

steps.title: But בְּמֹתָם is needed for another lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that בְּמֹתָם is not really extra. It is needed to teach that a שרץ makes things impure only while it is still moist, like at the time of its death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed to teach 'like at death': when moist they make things impure, and when dry they do not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. The word בְּמֹתָם already has a job of its own, so it is not free to teach the lesson about שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of אם אינו ענין only works if the word is truly extra. Here the גמרא says בְּמֹתָם teaches כעין מיתה: a שרץ makes things impure only while it is moist, as it was when it died, and not once it has dried out. If the word is already used for that, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It is still needed (for something else)
Similar to its state at death

phrases.english: But it is still needed
to teach 'similar to death':
when moist, they make things impure;
when dry, they do not make things impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that בְּמֹתָם is extra, which Step 11 depends on
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בְּמֹתָם is free to be applied to בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word already teaches the moist-versus-dry rule, so it is not extra and cannot be moved to another topic

steps.title: בְּמֹתָם is written twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בְּמֹתָם appears twice. One teaches the moist-versus-dry rule, and the other is free to teach the lesson about מיתה and שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In their death' is written twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that בְּמֹתָם appears two times. That gives one word for each lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One בְּמֹתָם teaches that only a moist שרץ makes things impure. The second בְּמֹתָם is still extra, so it can be applied to בהמה. It teaches that מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off and שחיטה does not, so רבא's proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that מיתה makes a limb count as fallen off and שחיטה does not comes from the second, extra בְּמֹתָם. Since it cannot apply to שרצים, it is applied to בהמה.

phrases.english: Two "in their death" are written.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31 and ויקרא 11:32.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי בְּמֹתָם כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a repeated word, so each lesson gets its own source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בְּמֹתָם is used up by the moist-versus-dry rule
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two בְּמֹתָם; one teaches moist-versus-dry, and the other teaches the difference between מיתה and שחיטה

steps.title: The argument is only about a living fetus
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the מחלוקת in the משנה is only about the limb of a fetus that was alive. If the fetus was dead, everyone agrees that the שחיטה makes the limb count as fallen off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The argument is about the limb of a living fetus. But for the limb of a dead fetus, everyone agrees that slaughter makes it count as fallen off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the מחלוקת in the משנה about a fetus that stuck out its leg before its mother was slaughtered. רב חסדא limits that argument to a fetus that was still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about whether the limb that was sticking out has the טומאה of נבלה. רב חסדא says this argument is only when the fetus was alive. If the fetus was already dead, everyone agrees the שחיטה makes the limb count as if it had fallen off before.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting as fallen off (separated from the body)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about the limb of a living fetus,
phrases.notes: This is the fetus in the משנה that stuck out its leg before its mother was slaughtered.

phrases.english: but about the limb of a dead fetus,
everyone agrees slaughter makes it count as fallen off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּאֵבֶר דְּעוּבָּר חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the מחלוקת in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about a living fetus; with a dead fetus, everyone agrees שחיטה makes the limb count as fallen off

steps.title: The same argument applies to a dead fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees with רב חסדא. He says the same מחלוקת applies whether the fetus was alive or dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: Just as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a different view from רב חסדא. He holds that the argument in the משנה covers a dead fetus too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that with a dead fetus there is no argument. רבה says there is no such difference: רבי מאיר and חכמים argue in both cases in the same way.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
Just as there is a dispute in this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is the living fetus, and "that case" is the dead fetus.

phrases.english: so there is a dispute in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה אָמַר כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזֶה כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב חסדא's limit in Step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies the same way to a living fetus and a dead fetus

steps.title: A teaching about the eight-month-old seems to clash with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a בן שמונה חי and challenges it from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says its שחיטה does not purify it even though its kind does have שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an eight-month-old that is alive. But a ברייתא teaches: The eight-month-old proves it, since even though its kind can be slaughtered, its slaughter does not make it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a בן שמונה born alive and then raises a contradiction from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a בן שמונה is not purified by שחיטה, and the reason given there is that שחיטה is never stated for its kind. The ברייתא says the opposite about the reason: its kind does have שחיטה, yet its שחיטה still does not purify it. So the reason in the משנה seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby animal born after only eight months, which is not expected to live
In its kind (other animals of the same type)

phrases.english: An eight-month-old that is alive.
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה, which says its שחיטה does not make it pure.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The live eight-month-old will prove it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמִינוֹ שְׁחִיטָה –
phrases.english: for even though its kind has slaughter,
its slaughter does not make it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה about a בן שמונה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reason that a בן שמונה is not purified because שחיטה is not stated for its kind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says its kind does have שחיטה, yet its שחיטה still does not purify it, so the reason must be something else

steps.title: The ברייתא counts a kind that is permitted through its mother
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the ברייתא treats a בן שמונה as a kind that has שחיטה, because a fetus can be permitted through its mother's שחיטה. Our משנה's תנא does not accept that kind of reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The ברייתא holds that this kind of animal does have שחיטה, through its mother. Our תנא does not bring a challenge from a kind that is permitted only through its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא settles the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא from Step 16. He says the two תנאים disagree about what counts as a kind that has שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus inside its mother becomes permitted when the mother is slaughtered. The ברייתא counts that as the kind having שחיטה, so it can use the בן שמונה as a challenge. Our משנה's תנא says permission that comes through the mother does not make this a kind that has שחיטה, so for him the challenge does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Its kind (type of animal) has שחיטה
Through its mother, as part of the mother's שחיטה
Our תנא, the one in our משנה

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
its kind does have slaughter
by way of its mother,
phrases.notes: A fetus still inside becomes permitted when its mother is slaughtered.

phrases.english: but our tanna
does not bring a challenge from a kind permitted through its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: יֵשׁ בְּמִינוֹ שְׁחִיטָה אַגַּב אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: the two sources define 'a kind that has שחיטה' differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא contradict each other about the live בן שמונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא counts permission through the mother as the kind having שחיטה. Our משנה does not, so each source is consistent with its own view.

steps.title: How does the ברייתא know that a slaughtered טרפה is טהור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's תנא gets the rule that שחיטה purifies a טרפה, since he rejects the 'its kind has שחיטה' reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to this תנא who brings the challenge, where does he learn that a טרפה's שחיטה makes it טהור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the ברייתא's view. It is setting up an answer from a פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the בן שמונה to knock down the idea that 'its kind has שחיטה' explains why a slaughtered טרפה is טהור. Without that reason, he still needs some source for the rule that a slaughtered טרפה does not carry the impurity of a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it may not be eaten even after שחיטה
Makes it טהור (here: it is not impure like a נבלה)
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And according to this tanna who does bring the challenge,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of the ברייתא from Step 16.

phrases.english: that a tereifa's slaughter makes it pure
from where does he know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּפָרֵיךְ, טְרֵפָה דִּשְׁחִיטָתָהּ מְטַהַרְתָּהּ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 17: once the ברייתא rejects the 'kind' reasoning, it needs another source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source the ברייתא's תנא uses for the rule that שחיטה purifies a טרפה.

steps.title: The source is the word מן in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: He learns it from רב יהודה in the name of רב (some say from a ברייתא). The word מן in 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' means only some dead animals make things impure, and a slaughtered טרפה is one that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: The פסוק says 'And if some of the animal dies.' Some animals make things impure and some do not. Which one does not? A טרפה that was slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18 with a דרשה on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מן ('some of') narrows the rule. Not every dead animal carries the impurity of a נבלה, and the one left out is a טרפה that was slaughtered. So the ברייתא does not need the 'its kind has שחיטה' reasoning at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Some, part of (learned from the word מִן)
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns that a slaughtered טרפה is טהור from the word מן in the פסוק, not from the idea that its kind has שחיטה.

phrases.english: He derives it
from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
The verse says: "And if some of the animal dies,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: some animals make things impure
and some animals do not make things impure,
and which one is that?
That is a tereifa that one slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word מן in 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' leaves out a slaughtered טרפה from נבלה impurity.

steps.title: Slaughtering a live nine-month fetus inside its mother
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks: if someone reached into an animal and slaughtered a live nine-month fetus inside it, what is the law? The גמרא notes the question can be asked according to both רבי מאיר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא asked: If someone put his hand into an animal's womb and slaughtered a live nine-month fetus, what is the law? This can be asked according to רבי מאיר, and it can be asked according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. The גמרא says it works under both opinions and is setting up an explanation of each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fully developed fetus can be slaughtered once it is born, but here it is slaughtered while still inside its mother. The question is whether that שחיטה counts. The גמרא will now show why it is unclear under each view.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question that he did not settle
It can be asked (it is a question)

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya asked:
If one stuck his hand into the womb of an animal,
and slaughtered a live nine-month fetus,
what is the law?
It can be asked according to Rabbi Meir,
and it can be asked according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: הוֹשִׁיט אֶת יָדוֹ לִמְעֵי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a fetus slaughtered while still inside its mother.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether slaughtering a live nine-month fetus inside its mother is a valid שחיטה.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר might say the שחיטה does not work inside the mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a בן פקועה needs שחיטה, but maybe only once it has come out into the world. While it is still inside its mother, perhaps its own שחיטה does not permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be asked according to רבי מאיר: רבי מאיר said that a בן פקועה needs שחיטה only where it came out into the open air. But inside its mother, perhaps שחיטה does not permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one side of the question according to רבי מאיר. It shows a reason the שחיטה might not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a בן פקועה needs its own שחיטה. That could be because it is treated as a separate animal only once it is out in the world. If so, a שחיטה done while it is still inside the mother would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A live fetus found inside an animal after the mother was slaughtered
The open air of the world; outside its mother

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the side that leans toward 'the שחיטה does not work.' The גמרא has not decided the question here.

phrases.english: It can be asked according to Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said only
that a ben pekua requires slaughter —
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי מאיר's view in the משנה later in the פרק.

phrases.english: this applies only where
it came out into the open air of the world,
but while inside its mother —
slaughter does not permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר בֶּן פְּקוּעָה טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי מאיר side of רב הושעיא's question from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's rule that a בן פקועה needs שחיטה applies only after it has been born.

steps.title: The question from the side of the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: Maybe even the רבנן agree that the fetus can be permitted by its own שחיטה inside the mother, because the Torah made all four סימנים valid for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, even according to the רבנן, the Torah made four סימנים fit for this fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out רב הושעיא's question, this time from the view of the רבנן. It asks whether they might also allow the fetus's own שחיטה to work while it is inside its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that a nine-month fetus is permitted through its mother's שחיטה. The question is whether they also allow the fetus's own שחיטה inside the womb to work. If so, there are four valid סימנים: two of the mother and two of the fetus, and cutting either pair permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: The signs that must be cut in שחיטה: the windpipe and the food pipe
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Or perhaps, even according to the Rabbis,
the Merciful One made four simanim fit for it.
phrases.notes: The four are the mother's two and the fetus's own two, so cutting either pair works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in step 20. Step 21 gave the רבי מאיר side; this gives the רבנן side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to the רבנן, a fetus's own שחיטה inside its mother also permits it, alongside the mother's שחיטה.

steps.title: Proof from an animal born a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא brings the earlier משנה that speaks of an animal born a טרפה, which never had a time of fitness. If a fetus could be slaughtered in the womb, it would have had such a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא said: Come and hear. The משנה speaks of an animal born a טרפה from the womb. If a fetus can be slaughtered inside its mother, you find that this animal did have a time when it was fit, since a person could have reached in his hand and slaughtered it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניא tries to answer the question with an earlier משנה. That משנה assumes an animal born a טרפה never had a time when it was fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If slaughtering a fetus in the womb worked, there was a moment before the animal became a טרפה when someone could have reached in and slaughtered it properly. That moment would count as a שעת הכושר. Since the משנה says it never had one, it seems that slaughtering inside the womb does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after שחיטה
From the womb, meaning from birth
A time when the animal was fit

phrases.english: Rav Ḥananya said: Come and hear:
An animal that was born a tereifa from the womb,
phrases.notes: This quotes an earlier משנה, which treats such an animal as one that never had a time of fitness.

phrases.english: but if it were so,

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר,
phrases.english: you find that it did have a time of fitness,
since if he wanted, he could insert his hand and slaughter it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְיָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle רב הושעיא's question using an existing משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That slaughtering a fetus inside its mother does not work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that treats an animal born a טרפה from the womb as never having had a time of fitness.

steps.title: רבא: the animal was formed a טרפה from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבא says to read the משנה as an animal formed a טרפה in the womb, like one with five legs, so there was never a moment it could have been slaughtered while fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Read it as an animal that was formed a טרפה from the womb. You find this with an animal that has five legs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away רב חנניא's proof. He rereads the משנה so that it no longer says anything about slaughtering inside the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal was a טרפה from the moment it was formed, there was never a fit moment, even inside the womb. An animal with five legs is an example, since that defect existed from the very start. So the משנה fits either side of the question, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Was formed, from the very beginning of its development
An animal with five legs, which is a טרפה

steps.whatToRemember: The question of slaughtering a fetus inside its mother is left unresolved here. רבא shows the proof only works if the animal became a טרפה later, but the משנה can be read as one formed a טרפה from the start.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Teach it as: that was formed a tereifa from the womb,
and you find it with an animal that has five legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: תָּנֵי שֶׁנּוֹצְרָה טְרֵפָה מִן הַבֶּטֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 23 by rereading the משנה it relies on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The original question is left unanswered.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the animal was once healthy inside the womb. If it was formed a טרפה from the start, there was never a fit moment, no matter what the rule about slaughtering in the womb is.

steps.title: New משנה: a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal
steps.stepSummary: When someone slaughters an animal and finds inside it an eight-month fetus, alive or dead, or a dead nine-month fetus, he tears it open and removes its blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters an animal and finds in it an eight-month fetus, alive or dead, or a nine-month fetus that is dead, tears it open and removes its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a fetus found inside an animal after the mother was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the fetus is permitted through its mother's שחיטה, because it counts as part of her. That is why its blood is treated like the mother's blood, which is forbidden. So he must tear the fetus open and remove the blood before eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
An eight-month fetus, one not carried to full term
A nine-month fetus, one carried to full term

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "tears it and removes its blood" as a kind of שחיטה. The fetus is already permitted through its mother. Tearing it open is only to get rid of the forbidden blood.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters an animal

phrases.aramaic: וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי אוֹ מֵת,
phrases.english: and found in it an eight-month-old fetus, alive or dead,
or a nine-month-old fetus that is dead,
tears it and removes its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה, וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי אוֹ מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion about slaughtering a fetus is set aside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus found in a slaughtered animal (an eight-month fetus, alive or dead, or a dead nine-month fetus) must be torn open and have its blood removed.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: A live nine-month fetus needs its own slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If a live nine-month fetus is found, רבי מאיר says it needs its own שחיטה, and the rule of אותו ואת בנו applies to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found a live nine-month fetus inside, it needs to be slaughtered, and he is liable for slaughtering 'it and its young' on one day. This is the opinion of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case: a fully developed nine-month fetus found alive inside the slaughtered mother. רבי מאיר rules that it must be slaughtered on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, a live nine-month fetus counts as a complete animal of its own, so its mother's שחיטה does not permit it. Since it is its own animal and also the mother's child, slaughtering it on the same day as the mother breaks the איסור of אותו ואת בנו. This fits step 21, where רבי מאיר was quoted as saying a בן פקועה needs שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A nine-month fetus, fully developed and able to live
The prohibition against slaughtering an animal and its young on the same day
A fetus found inside a slaughtered animal

phrases.english: If he found a live nine-month fetus
phrases.notes: The fetus was found inside the animal he just slaughtered, the same setup as step 25.

phrases.english: it requires slaughter,
and one is liable for 'it and its young',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28. Here the mother was already slaughtered today, so slaughtering the fetus today breaks this איסור.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה from step 25 with the case of a live nine-month fetus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a live nine-month fetus needs its own שחיטה and is subject to אותו ואת בנו.

steps.title: The חכמים: The mother's slaughter permits the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say the mother's שחיטה permits even a live nine-month fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: the slaughter of its mother permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר about the live nine-month fetus. They say it does not need its own שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, even a fully formed, live fetus is still part of its mother as long as it is inside her. So when the mother is slaughtered, the fetus becomes permitted along with her. This is the dispute that steps 21 and 22 were asking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'purifies it'; here it means permits it to be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת about a live nine-month fetus. רבי מאיר says it is its own animal and needs its own שחיטה. The חכמים say the mother's שחיטה permits it.
steps.confusionAlert: מְטַהַרְתּוֹ literally means 'purifies it.' The mother's שחיטה frees the fetus from the טומאה of a נבלה and also makes it permitted to eat.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
the slaughter of its mother renders it permitted.
phrases.notes: Literally 'purifies it': the fetus does not count as a נבלה, and it may be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the mother's שחיטה permits even a live nine-month fetus, so it needs no שחיטה of its own.
